top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is the most mature and experimentally secure achievement on the slate: magic-wavelength trapping removes the dominant systematic for many atoms at once, 1e-18 fractional uncertainty has been reproduced and compared across independent laboratories, and it already enables physics (gravitational redshift over millimetres, bounds on varying constants and dark-matter couplings). The Katori (concept, first demonstration) and Ye (record accuracy and stability) allocation is as clean as the slate offers, and a citation limited to the lattice clock and its 1e-18 realisation avoids the comb and the redefinition of the second. P002 is next for opening a new field of matter, though the pairing mechanism is unsettled and the three-name allocation is complicated by Cao and the Lopes dos Santos theory; P003 is secure on the diffuse flux but has an unsettled credit question; no award is last because at least one mature, well-defined achievement exists.
recusal_note: During my PhD I spent a year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, and Jun Ye is at JILA in the same community; no collaboration, supervision or funding tie to Katori or Ye is apparent from my profile, so not recusal-level, but noted.
